newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Backers of Indonesia's Megawati freed after clash.
newsitem.headline: Backers of Indonesia's Megawati freed after clash.

text.p: All 18 supporters of ousted minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri, detained here in a clash with the army on Saturday in Indonesia's second city, had been released by early Sunday, a party official said.

Sucipto, head of the East Java branch faction of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) that still backs Megawati, condemned the attack on 500 party members who on Saturday marched on the offices their rival faction in Surabaya, East Java.

"Those that came did not bring weapons. They came to protest because up to now the government has been ignoring the aspirations of the mass of PDI members in East Java," Sucipto told a news conference on Sunday afternoon.
Party officials said six people were injured when the protest was dispersed by the troops on Saturday afternoon.

The PDI split after a government-backed congress in June elected deputy parliamentary speaker Surjadi to head the Christian-Nationalist party, ousting Megawati, the popular daughter of Indonesia's founding president Sukarno.
Megawati, who says the congress was illegal, maintains she is the party's rightful leader and she apparently still enjoys widespread support among party members.

On July 27, police sparked the worst rioting in more than 20 years in Jakarta after they forcefully evicted Megawati supporters from PDI headquarters, sparking disturbances in which at least five people died.

Protests by PDI party members opposing Surjadi's leadership have continued around the country since June with one group of Megawati supporters earlier this month marching on Surjadi's official residence in Jakarta and chaining its front gate.
Sucipto denied the protestors had attacked the military and thrown stones at the troops dispatched to protect the offices of the Surjadi faction.
"We were only throwing plastic bottles of water," said one.
Political analysts say there is concern about stability ahead of next year's general election in May and the possibility of rising protests from disaffected PDI members.
